newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau looks to booming HK to fill vacant flats.
newsitem.headline: Macau looks to booming HK to fill vacant flats.

text.p: A Macau legislator says he has found a solution to the glut of flats in the Portuguese-run enclave -- encourage visitors from neighbouring Hong Kong to move in by letting them stay as long as they like.

Vitor Ng, who has submitted a bill on his proposals to the enclave's legislature, told the Futuro de Macau newspaper on Wednesday that allowing Hong Kong residents to stay indefinitely was a "solution to the real-estate crisis".
Macau has about 150,000 residential units, official statistics show. Property developers say between 30,000 and 50,000 of them stand empty.
Hong Kong citizens can now stay in Macau which borders China's southern Guangdong province, for up to 90 days. But many Hong Kong visitors are day trippers headed for Macau's casinos.
Macau last year gave foreigners limited residency rights if they invest at least one million patacas (US$125,000), such as by buying property. The scheme has attracted only a few dozen applicants.
Ng also said his proposals would free up "local capital that could be used for other investments".

Macau, due to be handed back to China on December 20, 1999, has changed enormously in recent years as developers reclaimed huge amounts of land and erected rows of office buildings and houses, many of which remain vacant.
Nearby Hong Kong, reverting to Chinese rule this year, has no such problem. The British territory is in the midst of a property boom.

The luxury property market recently scaled another peak when a 2,973-square-foot duplex apartment in the upscale Repulse Bay area of Hong Kong island fetched HK$50 million (US$6.47 million) in a recent sale.
